ev.fc_amulet.title: Charm over the cradle
ev.fc_amulet.text: Your grandmother brought a charm to your cradle - a little knot whose contents she will not name. Your father frowns: "Better call a priest and have it blessed properly." Your parents must decide - that is, you must.
ev.fc_amulet.grandma.ok: The knot hung over the cradle. Grandmother nodded, satisfied, and never spoke of it again.
ev.fc_amulet.priest.ok: The priest said a prayer over you and took a few coins for his trouble. Your mother was at peace.
ev.fc_amulet.nothing.ok: Your father said: "A child needs milk and warmth, not knots." Nothing hung over the cradle.
ev.fc_amulet_kept.title: Grandmother's knot
ev.fc_amulet_kept.text: Going through an old chest, you found the very knot that hung over your cradle. Inside: a pinch of salt, a coal and a lock of grey hair. You tied it round your neck and have worn it ever since.
ev.fc_amulet_blessed.title: The old priest
ev.fc_amulet_blessed.text: The old priest stopped you by the temple: "I remember you - I blessed you in the cradle. A loud one you were." Since then he greets you first, and the neighbours notice.
ev.fc_wetnurse.title: No milk
ev.fc_wetnurse.text: After the birth your mother is weak and has too little milk - you cry at night. You could hire a wet nurse, ask a neighbour with a baby of her own, or feed you goat's milk.
ev.fc_wetnurse.nurse.ok: The wet nurse came with her own son. You grew up at the same breast - milk brothers.
ev.fc_wetnurse.neighbor.ok: The neighbour fed you alongside her own child and took no money. "We'll settle up some day," she said.
ev.fc_wetnurse.goat.ok: You were fed goat's milk from a horn. You grew up frail, but you grew.
ev.fc_milk_brother.title: Milk kin
ev.fc_milk_brother.text: The wet nurse's son, who shared your milk, came back to your parts. You had not met in years, but he knew you at once: "Milk kin is stronger than blood." Now you have a friend you can rely on.
ev.fc_neighbor_favor.title: A debt to the neighbour
ev.fc_neighbor_favor.text: The neighbour who once fed you has grown old and asked for help with the harvest. You worked for her a week for nothing. "We're settled," she said, and now the whole street speaks of you with respect.
ev.fc_gift.title: Gifts for the cradle
ev.fc_gift.text: Guests brought gifts, and by custom one is laid in the cradle "for fate": a wooden horse, a small sheathed knife, or a string of counting beads.
ev.fc_gift.horse.ok: The horse went into the cradle. "A restless one," the guests laugh.
ev.fc_gift.knife.ok: The sheathed knife lay at the head of the cradle. "Skilled hands," says grandfather.
ev.fc_gift.beads.ok: The counting beads rattled in your fist. "Will count better than a merchant," your father jokes.
ev.fc_gift_hands.title: Skilled hands
ev.fc_gift_hands.text: The master watched you work a long time and said: "You were born with those hands." Later your mother remembered the knife laid in your cradle - and everyone laughed about it for a long time.
ev.fc_gift_count.title: Counting in your head
ev.fc_gift_count.text: At the market a trader got his sums wrong, and you corrected him faster than he could count on his fingers. He laughed and gave you a coin "for the head". The counting beads from the cradle must have helped.
ev.fc_fortune.title: The fortune-teller at the gate
ev.fc_fortune.text: A wandering fortune-teller stopped at the gate and asked to see the baby. "I'll tell what awaits it," she says, holding out her hand for a coin.
ev.fc_fortune.listen.ok: The fortune-teller looked at you and said only: "Trouble will come by water - do not fear it." And she left.
ev.fc_fortune.pay.ok: For a coin she foretold you a long life, a full house and the neighbours' respect. Your mother was happy all evening.
ev.fc_fortune.chase.ok: Your father sent her away. She muttered something over her shoulder, but no one caught what.
ev.fc_prophecy.title: The fortune-teller's words
ev.fc_prophecy.text: The crossing went wrong - the boat was swept away and everyone screamed. And suddenly you remembered your mother's story about the fortune-teller: "trouble will come by water - do not fear it." You did not, and you all got out.
ev.fc_prophecy_paid.title: The promised fate
ev.fc_prophecy_paid.text: Your mother still tells guests the fortune-teller promised you a long life and a full house. You laugh - and quietly count how much of it has come true so far.
ev.fc_patron.title: Who will be your sponsor
ev.fc_patron.text: By custom a child needs an elder sponsor - someone to vouch for it before people and before {faith}. The choices are a rich neighbour, the old man at the temple, or a poor uncle on your mother's side.
ev.fc_patron.rich.ok: The rich neighbour agreed and gave a silver spoon. Your mother hid it away.
ev.fc_patron.elder: The old man at the temple
ev.fc_patron.elder.ok: The old man took you in his arms and was silent a long time. "This one needs letters," he said at last.
ev.fc_patron.uncle.ok: Your uncle had nothing to give, but he wept for joy. "I won't leave you," he promised.
ev.fc_patron_rich.title: Your sponsor's word
ev.fc_patron_rich.text: The rich neighbour, your sponsor since the cradle, remembered you: he put in a word where it mattered and gave you money "for a start". "I promised to vouch for you - so I do."
ev.fc_patron_elder.title: The old man's lessons
ev.fc_patron_elder.text: The old man at the temple, who became your sponsor long ago, called you in and began teaching you to read and count in the evenings. "I promised you would have letters," he said.
ev.fc_betrothal.title: A cradle betrothal
ev.fc_betrothal.text: The neighbours came with food: they too have a new baby and propose to betroth the children now - "so our families become kin". It is sometimes done.
ev.fc_betrothal.agree.ok: Your parents shook hands and drank to the future wedding. No one told you anything, of course.
ev.fc_betrothal.refuse.ok: Your father politely refused. The neighbours smiled, but left sooner than they meant to.
ev.fc_betrothal.later.ok: "Let them grow up, then we'll see," said your mother. Everyone agreed it was wise.
ev.fc_betrothal_due.title: The old betrothal
ev.fc_betrothal_due.text: The neighbours reminded everyone of the betrothal made at your cradle. It caught you off guard: so your fate was decided before you could walk. Your parents say a word must be kept.
ev.fc_betrothal_grudge.title: An old grudge
ev.fc_betrothal_grudge.text: The neighbours never forgave the refusal they got at your cradle. Their son now picks on you at every chance, and his mother says behind your back that your family thinks too much of itself.
ev.fc_winter.title: A bitter winter
ev.fc_winter.text: The winter is so cold the water freezes indoors. A baby will not survive the cold. You could sell something valuable for fuel, move in with relatives who have a warm house, or endure.
ev.fc_winter.sell.ok: Your father sold the best thing in the house, and all winter the fire burned freely. You never coughed once.
ev.fc_winter.relatives.ok: All winter you lived with relatives: crowded and noisy, but warm. You were passed from arm to arm.
ev.fc_winter.endure.ok: Your mother warmed you with her own body night after night. You survived the winter, but the cough lasted until spring.
ev.fc_winter_story.title: The price of one winter
ev.fc_winter_story.text: One evening your father told how, in the year you were born, he sold the most valuable thing in the house so you would not freeze. "I don't regret a single day," he said. You lay awake a long time.
ev.fc_winter_cousins.title: Cousins
ev.fc_winter_cousins.text: That winter with the relatives bound the families for good. A cousin, laid in the same cradle as you when you were babies, became closer to you than a brother.
ev.fc_vow.title: A vow for the baby
ev.fc_vow.text: You were born weak and would not feed for a long time. In despair your mother wants to make a vow: that you will go on a pilgrimage when you are grown - or to give part of your money to the temple now.
ev.fc_vow.pilgrimage.ok: Your mother made the vow. A few days later you began to feed, and the household decided the vow had been heard.
ev.fc_vow.donate.ok: The money went to the temple. The priests promised to pray for you every day.
ev.fc_vow.none.ok: "We'll feed it ourselves," said grandmother, and set to work. You lived thanks to her.
ev.fc_vow_due.title: Keeping the vow
ev.fc_vow_due.text: Your mother reminded you: when you were a baby she vowed you would go on a pilgrimage. You set out. The road was long and costly, but you came home a different person.
ev.fc_vow_temple.title: The temple remembers
ev.fc_vow_temple.text: A priest at the temple found your name in the old records: "This child was prayed for every day." Now the temple treats you as one of its own.
